text:
Mia Chen: quick q — noticed inconsistent logprobs when a response hits max_tokens but also has a stop sequence. sometimes the last token has no logprob in the non-streaming response. anyone seen this?
Mia Chen: example request (simplified):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "foo",
  "stop": ["\n"],
  "max_tokens": 50,
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
Sam Ortiz: contract-wise we only promise logprobs for tokens that are returned in the final output. if the model is cut off by max_tokens you still returned N tokens so they should have logprobs. but streaming and truncation interactions are messy — could be a bug in the streamer that strips the last token's metadata.
Mia Chen: right — the full non-streaming JSON sometimes has "logprobs": null for the final token when stop+max collide. not always reproducible. saw it on canary yesterday.
Vijay Patel: I think this was a streaming-merge bug we fixed last month in runtime, but maybe it regressed for some models. we shouldn't change the external contract (i.e., what fields exist). fix should ensure metadata is preserved when assembling chunks. I'll check logs for canary-203.
Jordan Lee: I'll open a quick CR to add a unit + integration test. tests to add: (1) non-streaming stop hits max_tokens -> ensure last token has logprobs array, (2) streaming chunks merged -> same assertion. pinging @Sam for API wording.
Sam Ortiz: thanks — wording: "logprobs are provided for every token present in the returned text. If output is truncated by max_tokens, logprobs correspond to the returned tokens only." simple. add an explicit example in the docs.
Natalie Gomez: is this a breaking behavior for customers? cadence for changelog?
Mia Chen: some internal teams (search re-ranker) relied on last-token logprobs to detect truncation vs stop. they saw null and alerted. so it does hit customers but it's a bug not an intentional contract change.
Sam Ortiz: OK — since it's a bugfix (no API change) we should still notify customers: brief note in next status email + changelog entry. no version bump.
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary deploy started: canary-203 (runtime patch for streamer metadata)
Jordan Lee: CR: 4231 opened -> adds tests + a tiny doc snippet. will assign reviewers @Sam @Vijay. also adding a matrix test for temperature/top_p combos to avoid flaky determinism causing different truncation points.
Vijay Patel: good call on matrix. temperature/top_p can change tokenization boundaries because sampling variance affects whether a stop occurs before hitting max_tokens. add deterministic seeds for e2e so CI is stable.
Mia Chen: awesome — thx all. ping me when CR is ready and when canary finishes so I can rerun my repro harness. :eyes:
Sam Ortiz: FYI I updated the API doc PR template to remind authors to include a "token-level metadata on truncation" check. small doc change. :memo:
Jordan Lee: will merge after CI — aiming today. :shipit:
Mia Chen: thanks — and please tag me on the changelog blurb so I can add the internal impact note.
Vijay Patel: logging note — if we see truncated responses we emit a metric `response.truncated_by_max_tokens`. I'll add a dimension for "has_logprobs_missing" to help correlate.
